pattern.crimePattern: a young boda-fleet owner kills the car dealer who sold her a stolen pickup with a forged logbook and refused to refund her
pattern.notes: Fictional yard, bank and people. The forgery is shown only by its flaw (a chassis number that does not match the frame), never by how it was made.

ob.text: A cleaner reports the owner of Mathenge Motors, a second-hand car yard beside Karatina market, found dead in the yard office at 07:05. Ndirangu Mathenge (54). The gate was open when she arrived.

facts.text: Ndirangu Mathenge, owner of Mathenge Motors, was found dead in the yard office at 07:05; the gate was open.
He lay beside his desk; a steel steering-lock bar on the floor had been wiped.
The cash box under the desk is locked and untouched: KSh 31,000 inside.
Sales file: a white pickup sold on 12 January to Njeri Macharia for KSh 1.2 million, "sold as seen".
The sales file holds a copy of the logbook he gave Njeri for the white pickup.
A genuine logbook from the "VERIFIED" folder: same form and layout, its chassis number matching its car.
County trade licence: Mathenge Motors, partners N. Mathenge and W. Gachanja.
The trade licence is current and its number checks out with the county.
Wage book: Kiarie was paid in full to the end of March and signed for it.
The bay's car jack is on its hook, clean, with a dusty handle.
The gate's padlock is hanging open, not locked, with no forcing marks.
Gathua: a young woman in an orange reflective boda-fleet jacket went in through the yard gate at about 19:10 and came out fast at about 19:30.
Gathua sat at the market's side gate from 18:00 all night.
Gathua: nobody ever quarrels with the yard over parking; the lane is the market's, and the yard keeps to its fence.
Impound register: the white pickup was impounded on 14 March; the frame's chassis number differs from the logbook's by four characters, and belongs to a pickup stolen from Phyllis Nduta in Nairobi.
The impound register is the station's own, signed by the duty officer for every entry.
Njeri Express jackets: orange and reflective, "NJERI EXPRESS" on the back.
Njeri's loan: KSh 1.2 million "for a delivery pickup"; her first repayment was missed in March.
The bank confirms the loan number and its own stamp on the agreement.

Bar tab: Kiarie Ng'ang'a, Wednesday, 17:40–22:00.
The fundraiser hosts: Mzee Wahome gave a speech and stayed for the auction, 17:00–21:30.
Hotel register: Phyllis checked in at 16:00 and dined in the hotel restaurant 19:00–20:30.
Fingerprints taken from Njeri in detention.
Autopsy: one heavy blow from a straight steel bar.
Autopsy: death between 19:00 and 20:00.
Autopsy: no vehicle injuries, no other wounds, a sound heart.
Comparison view: the logbook's chassis number, dragged onto the frame photograph, differs in four characters.
Under the magnifier: the logbook's stamp is pressed ink with a halo, its lettering correctly spelled. A good copy.
Under the raking light: the signature has no pencil line beneath it. Not traced.
The logbook's registration date, 2019, is three years after the pickup's model year.
The seal is embossed in the paper, not photocopied.

reconstruction.text: In January Njeri buys a white pickup from Ndirangu with a business loan, to take her boda fleet into deliveries. "Sold as seen."

In March a roadblock at Sagana stops it. The frame's chassis number belongs to a pickup stolen from Phyllis Nduta in Nairobi; the logbook's has been altered. The pickup is impounded. Ndirangu won't refund her: "You bought it, you checked it."
Wednesday, 17:40. Kiarie leaves for the bar without locking the gate.
About 19:10, in her orange Njeri Express jacket, Njeri walks through the open gate to demand her money. He laughs. She picks up the steel steering-lock bar from his desk.
About 19:30 she comes out fast. Gathua, at the market's side gate, notices the jacket and thinks nothing of it.

clockPlan.note: One stamp: records on Njeri. Detain her at her base; the prints (6 h) and the logbook examination (10 h) both come back inside the 24 hours.
